answers.question: Question 1: A review found that rule R-07 is narrower than what you said: after a cancel call with no answer, you said that when the order read again shows it cancelled, the agent continues to the refund, but R-07 allows the refund only after the cancel call itself answered cancelled. Before: "The agent sends the refund call only after the cancel call answered cancelled. When the cancel call answers that the order has shipped since it was read, the agent says so, and sends no refund call." After: "The agent sends the refund call only after the cancel call answered cancelled, or after the order read again, following a cancel call with no answer, shows it cancelled. When the cancel call answers that the order has shipped since it was read, the agent says so, and sends no refund call." Do you accept the change?
answers.reply:
> Q4 If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order. Cancelled, continue to refund. Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation. Shipped, report it and issue no refund. Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> Note the race: status can flip processing → shipped between the agent's read and its cancel call; the store rejects the cancel and the agent must report that truthfully and issue no refund call.
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> 2. issue_refund adds outcome OrderNotCancelled.

answers.question: Question 2: A review found that rule R-10 never says what the agent tells the customer once the staff follow-up task is created, though the policy has the agent say store staff will follow up. Before, R-10 ends: "When the staff follow-up call times out, the agent sends it once more; when that also times out, it tells the customer to contact Harbor Goods support." After, it ends: "When the staff follow-up call answers created, the agent tells the customer what it knows about the order and the refund, and that store staff will follow up. When the staff follow-up call times out, the agent sends it once more; when that also times out, it tells the customer to contact Harbor Goods support." Do you accept the change?
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> 2. Cancel succeeded, refund call returned an error — refund not issued, state known; agent reports it, does not claim success, hands off to the store's manual refund process.
> 3. Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds. Final message must match the final refund status.
> Q2 How does the agent hand off to the manual refund process? Recommended (a): a state-changing handoff call, e.g. request_manual_refund(order_number, reason), creating a task for store staff.
> For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.
> Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> One handoff call covers both the failed-refund case and the unknown-cancellation case, with a reason argument.
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> 3. request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
> | Staff task queue | Takes the follow-up tasks the agent creates for store staff. | Harbor Goods | None. |

answers.question: Question 3: A review found that no rule says what the agent does when the cancel call answers order not found. Rule R-12, before: "The agent says the order is cancelled only when a cancel call answered cancelled or the order read again shows it cancelled, and states the refund as the order system shows it: its amount, the payment method and its status. It promises nothing about when the money arrives. When it cannot tell, it says so." After, the same with this sentence added: "When the cancel call answers order not found, it tells the customer the order was not found and changes nothing." Do you accept the change?
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> An order number matching none of the customer's orders: the agent says so and changes nothing.

answers.question: Question 4: A review found that no rule says what the agent does when the first read of the orders fails with an error, rather than timing out, before anything is proposed. (You said a read that times out is sent again with no limit, and for a re-read after a cancel or refund call you said what happens when it fails.) The shortest path: the customer asks to cancel; the agent reads the orders; the read fails. Rule R-01, before: "The agent reads and acts on only the signed-in customer's orders. When an order number matches none of them, it says so and changes nothing. When the order list call times out, it sends it again; the owner set no limit on this." After, the same with this sentence added: "When the order list call fails before anything is proposed, it tells the customer it cannot look up the orders right now and changes nothing." Do you accept the change?
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> 4. list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.
> For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.
> Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
